requirement:
During report conversion, on a terminal enabled under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.terminal`, Habeas MUST
display updating progress with elapsed time and completed and total
test-attempt counts. The total MUST count the recorded attempts selected for
conversion. An attempt MUST advance the completed count only after its
conversion has finished or reported a collection failure, including processing
its associated child-process profiles. These counts MUST measure conversion
work regardless of the attempt's test outcome.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress`. The terminal-enablement rules belong to `.progress.terminal`, which is cited context, so I did not reassess them.

Obligations and the tests that check them:

- **Updating display with elapsed time and completed/total counts.**
  - `src/execution_coverage/progress.rs#mod[tests]/fn[stage_and_conversion_counts_are_visible_then_cleared]` builds a conversion progress for totals 0 and 2 on a recording terminal.
  - It calls `completed()` and force-draws. It then asserts that the bar position equals the expected count, that the text contains `{n}/{total} attempts`, and that the text contains the `[00:00:` elapsed-time marker.
  - `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[coverage_progress_on_a_pty_preserves_reports_and_plain_output_policy]` checks the real binary on a PTY with `TERM=xterm`. The output contains `Converting coverage`, `1/1 attempts`, `[00:` and in-place escape sequences.
- **Total counts the recorded attempts selected for conversion.**
  - The PTY test selects a single test with `-E test(second)` and sees `1/1`. The fixture has more than one test, so this shows the total follows the selection rather than every test.
  - The unit test covers total 2 and total 0.
  - In `src/execution_coverage/runner.rs#fn[finish]`, `Progress::conversion(attempts.len())` is created from the attempts collected there. This is the source of the total.
- **An attempt advances the count only after its conversion finishes or reports a collection failure.** This includes processing child-process profiles.
  - `src/execution_coverage/runner.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parallel_conversion_is_bounded_and_retains_every_result_in_order]` runs 8 items on 2 workers.
  - The completion callback asserts that `finished[index]` is already set. That is the "progress advanced before conversion finished" check.
  - One item returns `Err("unreadable profile")`, and `completed` still reaches 8.
  - In `fn[finish]`, `finish_attempt` is the conversion closure and `progress.completed()` is the completion callback. The ordering test therefore covers the real wiring, including child-process profile handling inside `finish_attempt`.
  - The PTY test's `test(child_process)` case (2 processes) and `test(missing_profile)` case (0 processes, collection failure with the "partial profiles and reports have been retained" diagnostic) both run end to end.
  - `fn[empty_conversion_starts_no_work_and_reports_no_completions]` covers the empty case.
- **Counts measure conversion work regardless of test outcome.**
  - The PTY test runs success (`second`, `child_process`), failed (`deliberate_failure`) and collection-failure (`missing_profile`) attempts. Each case asserts that the conversion progress is cleared.
  - The runner test shows failed conversions still advance the count.

No unacknowledged gap found. The one thing the tests don't pin down is an exact multi-attempt total through the real binary. The unit test with total 2 and the `attempts.len()` wiring cover it adequately.

text: During report conversion, on a terminal enabled under
display updating progress with elapsed time and completed and total
test-attempt counts. The total MUST count the recorded attempts selected for
conversion. An attempt MUST advance the completed count only after its
conversion has finished or reported a collection failure, including processing
its associated child-process profiles. These counts MUST measure conversion
work regardless of the attempt's test outcome.
Habeas coverage progress MUST be displayed when stderr is an interactive
terminal and `TERM` is not `dumb`. `NO_COLOR` MUST disable color without
disabling progress. When stderr is redirected or `TERM=dumb`, Habeas coverage
progress MUST NOT emit animation or terminal control sequences.
Temporary progress displays MUST be cleared when their stage ends, including
empty work and early collection failures. Final diagnostics and the coverage
artifact location MUST remain readable. Progress reporting MUST NOT change
coverage results, retained profiles, or command exit status.
